title: Minerals & rock identification
examples: How can I tell if a rock is a mineral?
What is the Mohs scale for hardness?
What other properties can I use to identify a rock?

explain.say: Today we are learning to identify minerals and rocks. We will look at their physical properties. These properties help us tell them apart.
One important property is hardness. Hardness measures how easily a mineral can be scratched. We use the Mohs scale to test this.
Another property is streak. The streak is the color of the mineral's powder. You can test this by rubbing it on a streak plate.
Luster describes how shiny a mineral looks. Some minerals have a metallic luster, like shiny metal. Others have a glassy luster, like quartz.
Rocks are made up of minerals, but they are not single minerals. We can identify rocks by grouping their mineral components. For example, granite is a common rock.
In real life, you might use these properties to check gemstones. A jeweler needs to know the hardness to ensure the stone will last. Diamond is very hard.

faq.q: How do I know if a rock is a mineral?
faq.a: A mineral must be naturally occurring and have a definite chemical structure. Rocks are made up of one or more minerals.
asks: Are rocks always made of minerals?
What is the difference between a rock and a mineral?

faq.a: The Mohs scale measures the relative scratch resistance of minerals. It ranks minerals from softest to hardest using natural minerals for testing.
asks: Is the Mohs scale for rocks or minerals?
How do I use the Mohs scale?

faq.q: What is the best way to test for streak?
faq.a: You should always use a clean streak plate for this test. You rub the mineral across the plate to see the color of the powder left behind.
asks: Can I use my fingers to test the streak?
What should the streak look like?

faq.q: Is color always a reliable identifier?
faq.a: No, color is not reliable on its own because many different minerals can look the same color. You need to check other properties too.
asks: Can I only use color to identify rocks?
Are there minerals that are naturally colored?

faq.q: What is the difference between luster and shine?
faq.a: Luster is the general term for how shiny a mineral appears. It describes the quality of light reflection, like glassy or metallic.
asks: Is luster the same as shine?
What are the types of luster?

facts: Minerals are naturally occurring, inorganic solids with a crystal structure.
The Mohs scale ranks mineral hardness from one to ten.
Streak is the color of a mineral in powdered form, tested on a streak plate.
Luster describes how light reflects off the surface of a mineral.

quiz.say: A mineral scratches glass, but glass does not scratch it. Which property is being tested?
quiz.why: Hardness directly measures the ability of one mineral to scratch another material.

wrong.0: Luster only tells you how shiny the surface looks.
wrong.1: Color can change or be misleading when testing.
wrong.3: Streak is about the color of the powder, not scratching ability.

quiz.say: You rub a mineral on a plate and a reddish-brown powder appears. What property did you test?
quiz.why: The color of the powder left after rubbing is called the streak.

wrong.1: Luster describes the surface shine, not the powder color.
wrong.3: While related, streak is specifically the powder color.

quiz.say: A mineral shines like polished metal and is very hard. Which combination of properties describes it?
quiz.why: Metallic luster describes the shine, and high hardness means it resists scratching.

wrong.0: This would describe something shiny like glass but soft, like talc.
wrong.1: Dull luster means it does not shine, even if it is very hard.
wrong.2: This combination suggests something shiny but easily scratched.
